idiomatic: Cui Cheng, Wang Xian, Feng Yi

idiomatic: Biographies 12: Cui Cheng

literal: (Son Yi; grandson Yu; great-grandson Jiong
idiomatic: (Son Yi; grandson Yu; great-grandson Jiong

literal: (Xiu, five generations later, six generations later: Zhan, Biao
idiomatic: (Xiu; five generations on, six generations on: Zhan, Biao

literal: (Cheng's elder brother Sui; Wang Xian
idiomatic: (Cheng's elder brother Sui; Wang Xian

literal: (Great-grandsons Xin, Xi, Hao; Feng Yi
idiomatic: (Great-grandsons Xin, Xi, Hao; Feng Yi

literal: (Clan great-grandson Hui; Hui's son Longzhi; Hui's younger brother Su; clan younger cousin Shu)
idiomatic: (Clan great-grandson Hui; Hui's son Longzhi; Hui's younger brother Su; clan younger cousin Shu)

literal: Cui Cheng, styled Shuzu, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, fifth-generation descendant of Wei Commandant of Justice Yan.
idiomatic: Cui Cheng, styled Shuzu, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe — fifth in descent from Yan, Commandant of Justice under Wei.

literal: His great-grandfather Liang was Jin Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Liang had been Jin Director of the Secretariat.

literal: His grandfather Yu served the Shi clan as Special Grand Master.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served the Later Zhao as Special Grand Master.

literal: His father Yu was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: His father Yu held office as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

literal: Cheng from youth loved learning and had literary talent.
idiomatic: From boyhood Cheng loved books and showed real literary gift.

literal: He served Murong Jun, was made Aide in the Bureau of Writings, and compiled the Records of Yan.
idiomatic: Under Murong Jun he became Aide in the Bureau of Writings and compiled the Records of Yan.

literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

literal: When Jun fell, Fu Jian made him Administrator of Qi commandery.
idiomatic: When Jun's state collapsed, Fu Jian appointed him Administrator of Qi.

literal: After Fu Jian's defeat he entered Jin service and successively governed Qinghe and Pingyuan.
idiomatic: After Jian's ruin he entered Jin service and in turn governed Qinghe and Pingyuan.

literal: Captured by Zhai Liao, he was made Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Zhai Liao took him captive and made him Director of the Secretariat.

literal: When Murong Chui destroyed Zhai Zhao, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: When Murong Chui destroyed Zhai Zhao, he became Supervisor of the Secretariat.

literal: When Murong Bao fled east to Helong, Cheng remained at the rear capital as Minister of the Civil Service.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao fled east to Helong, Cheng stayed behind as Minister of the Civil Service.

literal: When Murong Lin acceded, Cheng brought wife and children and returned to Wei.
idiomatic: When Murong Lin took the throne, Cheng brought wife and children home to Wei.

literal: Zhang Gun had praised him first; hence Daowu treated him with great favor.
idiomatic: Zhang Gun had praised him first, and Daowu therefore favored him richly.

literal: He was appointed Minister of the Secretariat, recorded the affairs of the thirty-six bureaus, was given separate clerks, and dwelt in the Gate Office.
idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Secretariat, oversaw all thirty-six bureaus with his own clerks, and lodged in the Gate Office.

literal: Soon after he was made Imperial Censor.
idiomatic: Soon after he became Imperial Censor.

literal: Daowu besieged Zhongshan without taking it; the six armies lacked grain and he asked Cheng for counsel.
idiomatic: Daowu besieged Zhongshan without success; the armies ran short of grain, and he asked Cheng's counsel.

literal: Cheng said: "When the flying owl eats mulberries its cry changes — the Odes praise the matter; mulberries may be taken to supplement grain.
idiomatic: Cheng said, "The flying owl eats mulberries and its cry changes — the Odes mark the thing. Mulberries could help feed the army."

literal: " Though the Emperor resented his insolence, the troops needed food, and he allowed mulberries to be taken in lieu of rent.
idiomatic: The Emperor bridled at the insolence, yet the troops needed food — so mulberries were accepted in place of rent.

literal: Cheng added: "Soldiers could gather them in season; after the season they fall and are gone."
idiomatic: Cheng added that soldiers should gather them in season, "for afterward they drop and are wasted."

literal: The Emperor raged: "With rebels within not yet subdued, how may soldiers doff armor to pick mulberries!"
idiomatic: The Emperor flared: "Rebels within are not yet crushed — shall soldiers strip armor to pick mulberries?"

literal: Because Zhongshan was still untaken, he did not punish him.
idiomatic: Zhongshan still held out, so no punishment followed.

literal: When Yao Xing invaded Jin, the garrison commander of Xiangyang, Xi Hui, sent a swift messenger begging troops from the Prince of Changshan, Zun; the letter read, "Your worthy elder brother strides in martial glory through the Central Plains."
idiomatic: When Yao Xing struck Jin, Xi Hui at Xiangyang sent a rider begging aid from Prince of Changshan Zun; the letter said, "Your worthy elder brother strides in arms through the Central Plains."

literal: Daowu judged this a breach of the bond between ruler and subject and ordered Cheng and Zhang Gun to draft Zun's reply to the envoy, also demoting the addressee's sovereign title in the response.
idiomatic: Daowu called this a breach of ruler and subject and ordered Cheng and Gun to draft Zun's reply — and to demote the Jin ruler's title in it.

literal: Cheng and Gun wrote the letter and used only "Your exalted lord."
idiomatic: Cheng and Gun wrote back with merely "Your exalted lord."

literal: The Emperor, furious at missing the point, demoted Gun and had Cheng put to death.
idiomatic: The Emperor, furious they had missed his intent, demoted Gun and sentenced Cheng to death.

literal: Later Jin's Inspector of Jingzhou, Sima Xiuzhi, and several dozen others driven out by Huan Xuan were all coming to surrender.
idiomatic: Later Sima Xiuzhi, Inspector of Jingzhou, and dozens more expelled by Huan Xuan were all fleeing north to surrender.

literal: At Chenliu they heard Cheng had been killed and split into two bands: one fled to Chang'an, one to Guanggu.
idiomatic: At Chenliu they heard Cheng was dead and split: one band ran to Chang'an, one to Guanggu.

literal: When the Emperor heard, he deeply regretted it; thereafter when scholars erred they were often treated leniently.
idiomatic: The news filled the Emperor with bitter regret; thereafter scholars who stumbled were usually spared harshly.

literal: Cheng's sons were Yi, Wei, Yan, and Yi.
idiomatic: Cheng's sons were Yi, Wei, Yan, and Yi.

literal: At first, when Cheng moved inward, he always feared he would not escape harm; he sent his wife Lady Zhang and four sons back to Murong De at Guanggu, keeping only his youngest, Yi, at Dai.
idiomatic: When Cheng first moved inward he feared he could not escape ruin; he sent Lady Zhang and four sons to Murong De at Guanggu and kept only young Yi at Dai.

literal: When Cheng died, this too was held against him.
idiomatic: When Cheng died, even that was counted against him.

literal: Yi, styled Taichong, was Regular Attendant at the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Marquis of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Yi, styled Taichong, became Regular Attendant at the Secretariat and Marquis of Qinghe.

literal: Taiwu heard that Song had made his elder brother Shen Inspector of Ji and said: "Yilong employs his brother — do I lack land in Ji?"
idiomatic: Taiwu heard Song had made his brother Shen Inspector of Ji and said, "Yilong uses his brother — have I no Ji province?"

literal: " He thereupon made Yi Inspector of Ji.
idiomatic: He promptly made Yi Inspector of Ji.

literal: He entered court as Grand Herald and, bearing credentials, invested Yang Nandang as King of Southern Qin.
idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Herald and, with credentials, invested Yang Nandang as King of Southern Qin.

literal: On missions he returned again and again, spreading the court's renown; Taiwu was pleased.
idiomatic: On repeated embassies he bore the court's dignity abroad; Taiwu approved.

literal: Later he went with the adept Wei Wenxiu to Mount Wangwu to compound the golden elixir, but did not succeed.
idiomatic: Later he went with adept Wei Wenxiu to Mount Wangwu to seek the golden elixir and failed.

literal: At the start of the Zhenjun era he died.
idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Zhenjun era.

literal: At first Cui Hao, Yi, and Mo, Administrator of Xingyang, were nearly the same age.
idiomatic: Cui Hao, Yi, and Mo of Xingyang were nearly of an age.

literal: Hao was eldest, then Mo, then Yi.
idiomatic: Hao was eldest, Mo next, Yi last.

literal: The three traced to different ancestors, but Mo and Yi were close kin.
idiomatic: They sprang from different lines, yet Mo and Yi were close kin.

literal: Hao relied on his family's generations of Wei and Jin high office and often insulted Mo and Yi.
idiomatic: Hao leaned on generations of Wei and Jin grandees and often belittled Mo and Yi.

literal: Hao did not believe in Buddhism; Mo was deeply devoted — even in filth he would bow to images.
idiomatic: Hao scorned the Buddha; Mo was devout and would bow to images even in filth.

literal: Hao laughed loudly: "To kneel in unclean places with that head of yours — to these barbarian gods!"
idiomatic: Hao laughed: "You kneel your head in filth before barbarian gods!"

literal: " Mo once told others: "Taojian may deceive me — how dare he slight my Zhou'er!"
idiomatic: Mo once said, "Taojian may fool me — how dare he slight my Zhou'er!"

literal: " Hao's childhood name was Taojian; Yi's was Zhou'er.
idiomatic: Hao's pet name was Taojian; Yi's was Zhou'er.

literal: Taiwu heard much of this; hence when Hao was executed both their houses were spared.
idiomatic: Taiwu heard of it; when Hao was executed both families were spared.

literal: Yi had five sons.
idiomatic: Yi had five sons.

literal: The youngest, Rui, was executed for trafficking with foreign lands.
idiomatic: The youngest, Rui, was executed for dealing with outsiders.

literal: From Cheng's death to Rui's execution, three generations and more than fifty years — the northern branch of the house was ended.
idiomatic: From Cheng's death to Rui's execution three generations and fifty years passed — the northern line was extinguished.

literal: Yu, styled Wenruo, was grandson of Wei's son through Yi's elder brother Wei.
idiomatic: Yu, styled Wenruo, was grandson of Wei, son of Yi's elder brother Wei.

literal: His father Xunzhi, styled Ningguo, held Grand Marshal and Outer Troops Officer, posthumously made Direct Attendant.
idiomatic: His father Xunzhi, styled Ningguo, reached Grand Marshal and Outer Troops Officer and was posthumously made Direct Attendant.

literal: Yu and his elder brother Xiangru both came from Song into Wei.
idiomatic: Yu and elder brother Xiangru both entered Wei from Song.

literal: Xiangru was known for talent and learning and died young.
idiomatic: Xiangru was famed for learning and died young.

literal: Yu in youth met a recluse monk who taught him the Plain Questions and the A and B Canon of Acupuncture; he became skilled in medicine.
idiomatic: In youth Yu met a recluse monk who taught the Plain Questions and the A–B Canon; he mastered medicine.

literal: The son of Prince of Zhongshan Ying, Zilue, once fell ill; Wang Xian and others could not cure him.
idiomatic: Prince Ying's son Zilue fell ill; Wang Xian and others could not heal him.

literal: Yu needled him; at withdrawal of the needle he recovered — later he was Aide of Ji.
idiomatic: Yu needled him; the needle scarcely left before he was well — later he became Aide of Ji.

literal: By nature he was kind and forgiving; seeing the afflicted, he delighted to treat them.
idiomatic: Kind by nature, he delighted to treat whoever was sick.

literal: He widely taught disciples and had many save lives through treatment.
idiomatic: He taught many pupils and sent them out to heal.

literal: Among his pupils, Zhao Yue of Qinghe and Hao Wenfa of Bohai and others also won names.
idiomatic: Pupils such as Zhao Yue of Qinghe and Hao Wenfa of Bohai won names in turn.

literal: Yu's son Jingzhe was bold and open — also famed in medicine.
idiomatic: Yu's son Jingzhe was bold and open, likewise famed in medicine.

literal: Serving Wei, he was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Chief Clerk of the Minister of State.
idiomatic: In Wei he was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Chief Clerk to the Minister of State.

literal: Jingzhe's son Jiong, styled Fajun, from youth loved learning, ranged through classics and commentaries, had many arts, and was especially skilled in physiognomy.
idiomatic: Jingzhe's son Jiong, styled Fajun, loved learning from youth, ranged the classics, mastered many arts, and excelled at physiognomy.

literal: In Wei he was Aide to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: In Wei he served as Aide to the Minister of Works.

literal: At the start of Qi Tianbao he was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.
idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao's opening he became Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.

literal: He successively was Administrator of Gaoyang and Household Master of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: He was in turn Administrator of Gaoyang and Household Master of the Heir Apparent.

literal: In the Wuping era he was Regular Attendant and Acting Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: In Wuping he was Regular Attendant with acting protocol equal to the Three Dukes.

literal: On an imperial visit to Jinyang he once told Secretariat Vice Director Li Delin: "These days I have read the physiognomies of civil and military officers down from the High Chancellor — all to the end of their fate; I cannot bear to speak it."
idiomatic: At Jinyang he told Li Delin, "I have read the faces of every officer down from the High Chancellor — each to the end of his fate; I cannot speak it aloud."

literal: "Only my younger brother should grow richer still — in another state, not this court; I shall not live to see it."
idiomatic: Only my brother will grow richer still — in another realm, not this one; I shall not see it."

literal: " Such was his precision.
idiomatic: So keen was his art.

literal: Jiong was frugal and careful, cultivated modesty, and always shared salary with kin and friends.
idiomatic: Jiong was frugal and careful, cultivated humility, and divided every stipend among kin and friends.

literal: He ended as Grand Herald.
idiomatic: He died as Grand Herald.

literal: On his deathbed he admonished his two sons: "Modesty and thrift are the carriage of blessing; pride and extravagance the engine of disaster."
idiomatic: Dying, he told his sons, "Modesty and thrift are the carriage of blessing; pride and waste the engine of ruin."

literal: "Those who ride the carriage of blessing grow ever healthier; those who tread the engine of disaster topple in a moment — take heed!"
idiomatic: Those who ride blessing grow ever sound; those who tread ruin topple in a breath — heed me!"

literal: "After I am gone, bury me in seasonable dress; offer no sacrificial beasts; let the coffin only enclose the corpse and the grave not leak — that is all."
idiomatic: Bury me in proper season's dress; no sacrificial beasts; a coffin that only wraps the corpse; a grave that does not gape — no more."

literal: " When he died, the eldest son Xiu followed his command.
idiomatic: When he died, eldest son Xiu obeyed.

literal: Jingzhe's younger brother Jingfeng, styled Luanshu, was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.
idiomatic: Jingzhe's brother Jingfeng, styled Luanshu, was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.

literal: Xiu, styled Huisheng.
idiomatic: Xiu, styled Huisheng.

literal: His great-grandfather Shen served Song as Inspector of Qing and Ji.
idiomatic: Great-grandfather Shen served Song as Inspector of Qing and Ji.

literal: His grandfather Linghe was Song Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Grandfather Linghe was Song Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

literal: His father Zongbo first returned to Wei and was posthumously made Administrator of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Father Zongbo first came home to Wei and was posthumously made Administrator of Qinghe.

literal: Xiu in youth was orphaned and poor yet stood upright by sheer will.
idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, Xiu stood upright by will alone.

literal: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he entered the capital and became close friends with Song Bian and Xing Luan.
idiomatic: As a cultivated talent he entered the capital and grew intimate with Song Bian and Xing Luan.

literal: Minister Wang Yi admired his reputation, married his eldest son to Xiu's sister, and supported him with goods — thus he briefly revived.
idiomatic: Wang Yi of the Secretariat admired him, married his heir to Xiu's sister, and supplied goods so his fortunes briefly rose.

literal: Xiaowen took Xiu's sister as a consort.
idiomatic: Xiaowen took Xiu's sister into the inner palace.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Regular Attendant at the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Acting Regular Attendant at the Secretariat.

literal: Xiu studied hard; in the gaps of public business and campaigns his hand never left the scroll.
idiomatic: He studied relentlessly; between office and campaign his hand never left a scroll.

literal: His honors stood just below Song Bian and Guo Zuo.
idiomatic: Court favor ranked him just below Bian and Zuo.

literal: On Xiaowen's southern campaign, Prince of Beihai Xiang was made Vice Director of the Secretariat to command the rear capital; Xiu was made Left Assistant Director.
idiomatic: On Xiaowen's southern expedition, Prince Xiang of Beihai commanded the rear capital; Xiu became Left Assistant Director.

literal: An edict said Beihai was young and the hundred offices' business heavy — authority was therefore entrusted to Xiu.
idiomatic: An edict said the prince was young and business crushing — power was lodged with Xiu.

literal: He was made Chief Clerk, also Acting Regular Attendant, and helped fix ritual.
idiomatic: He became Chief Clerk and Acting Regular Attendant and helped settle ritual.

literal: The Emperor once examined the old storehouse, found an ancient cap, and read the inscription: "Made by Southern Minister Cui Cheng."
idiomatic: The Emperor once searched the old treasury, found an ancient cap inscribed, "Made by Southern Minister Cui Cheng."
